review_notes:
I read the whole file (lines 1–223) with the simp rubric in mind. It has no @[simp] declarations and no simp-set definitions. The only simp uses are `simp only`/`simp_rw` calls with explicit lemma lists, and one bare `simp` closing the empty-set case. I found no rewrite cycles, no unwanted expansion and no competing rules.

The main lemmas are iff or implication statements with non-trivial hypotheses. `withDensity_eq_iff_of_sigmaFinite` and `withDensity_eq_iff` need measurability and finiteness assumptions, and they relate two measures to an a.e. equality of functions, so they are not canonical simp rewrites. `ae_const_le_iff_forall_lt_measure_zero` and `ae_le_const_iff_forall_gt_measure_zero` turn an a.e. statement into a quantified statement. That direction is a deliberate choice and is not a clear normal form. Adding simp attributes to any of these would be speculative and could cause unwanted expansion.

I did not search other files for downstream uses. I did not run Lean, so I have no experimental evidence either way.
